title: Caddy rewrite can decode file path information twice and bypass path-based restrictions
summary: The rewrite handler inserted a decoded file-matcher remainder without escaping it, after which the rewritten URI was percent-decoded again. On configurations using try_files, split_path, and a rewrite with that remainder, a double-encoded path can bypass an earlier path-based deny matcher and expose static files; reserved characters can also alter the path or query. The advisory demonstrates the behavior and limits applicability to that configuration pattern.
ai_role: The primary Caddy advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-32RAL55Q. Anthropic’s primary scanner page describes an AI model-based scanning service and the Oct 8 launch post identifies Claude Mythos among its strongest models. The item-specific model is unspecified.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-69hv-5jfc-mvmv on 2026-11-04 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-32RAL55Q); no CVE was assigned in the advisory.
remediation_note: Caddy 2.11.8 escapes the file-matcher remainder while preserving slashes before parsing the rewritten URI.

impacts.conditions: Requires the Caddy rewrite/try_files configuration using the file remainder placeholder; attacker supplies crafted path info.
impacts.exploitation: The cited advisory does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.
